newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down,yen firmer before trade data.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down,yen firmer before trade data.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended with losses on Tuesday, slipping on the strengthening yen against the dollar, brokers said. They said investors were sidelined ahead of Japan's May customs-cleared trade data due Wednesday and the G7 summit later this week.
The Nikkei 225 ended 87.41 points or 0.42 percent down at 20,593.66. Its September futures shed 220 to finish at 20,600.

"Trade was rather featureless apart from the fact that major exporters were weak as the yen was a bit stronger," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager. "Cautious investors concentrated on trade in individual issues."
Turnover was a modest 399 million shares, up slightly from Monday's 315 million. Losers beat winners 630 to 427, while 187 issues were steady.
The yen rose slightly, hovering around 113 yen to the dollar for most of the session compared to about 114 yen on Monday.

Market participants were bracing for turbulence in currencies by backing away from shares in the high-tech and car sectors, brokers said. This could be sparked by trade data revealing a rise in Japan's trade surplus ahead of the Denver G7 summit.
"There is too much uncertainty in the air over currencies," said a foreign trader. "Electricals have risen almost 15 percent in this quarter alone and are in need of correction."
Sony Corp shed 110 yen to close at 9,800.
Banks, which had risen due to short-covering by hedge funds in recent sessions, lost momentum.

But Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd surged after news on Monday that it had agreed with Barclays Bank to begin discussions on several areas of cooperation. Hokkaido Takushoku rose 26 yen to 170 yen in the heaviest turnover on the first section of the Tokyo bourse of 16.22 million shares.
Hokkaido Bank Ltd, which will merge with Hokkaido Takushoku in 1998, also jumped, adding 23 yen or 16.13 percent to 164, making it the third largest percentage gainer.

"It's a sad thing that Japan's banks, not to mention banking sector shares, can only be revived with help from foreigners," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "But the banks are better off with their help than without."

Sumitomo Bank stumbled on reports that two loan examiners have filed suit against its unit in California for compensation for losses they say they suffered after refusing to go along with the bank's senior managers in extending loans.
Shares of Sumitomo Bank closed down 80 yen at 1,770, after earlier hitting a low of 1,750.
A Sumitomo spokeswoman in Tokyo told Reuters that Sumitomo Bank of California had dismissed the claims as groundless.
"Sumitomo's shares weakened in the afternoon session," a trader at a foreign brokerage said. "It seems that the report has some investors worried."
Some brokers added that the downward revision in Sumitomo's shares from "average performer" to "underperformer" by Goldman Sachs late last week could also have contributed to the losses.

Amid anxiety over currencies, domestic-demand driven shares continued to gain, with credit/lease at the top of the gaining sectors list. It was followed by warehouses, communication, sea transport and fisheries.
Takefuji Corp, Japan's largest consumer financing firm, renewed its calendar year high, rising to 6,320 yen at one point. In late Tokyo, it was up 220 yen at 6,270.

"In the OTC market, foreign investors continue to be net buyers, seeking large capital issues with solid earnings and low PERs. Takefuji fits the description," a broker at a second tier brokerage said.
Declining sectors were headed by rubber, services, precision instruments, oil and insurance.

"From a technical point of view, the Nikkei average should be gaining but the wait-and-see mood is thick and gains are hard to accumulate," said Kenji Karikomi, Daiwa Securities deputy general manager. "Profit-taking moves are strong over 20,500."

The TOPIX index fell 4.81 points or 0.31 percent to 1,537.38. The Nikkei 300 shed 1.37 points or 0.46 percent to 297.13. The second section index was up 7.30 points or 0.40 percent at 1,833.52. --Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk
